policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's 'to tread them down' and the Hebrew gloss 'to make them a treading down' do not distinguish the qere spelling וּלְשׂוּמוֹ from the ketiv ולשימו; both readings remain compatible, so the documented qere base remains the fallback.

ASV's 'their treasures' does not distinguish the qere וַעֲתוּדוֹתֵיהֶם from the ketiv ועתידתיהם, and the note 'the inhabitants' is classed alternative_rendering and therefore cannot decide the textual reading; both remain compatible and the qere base remains the fallback.

ASV reads 'the daughter of Zion,' selecting בַּת (r00-base); the mapped textual_variant note explicitly identifies 'house' as another reading, which is the ketiv alternative rather than the wording rendered by ASV.
